name: microduck-stand
$comment: The microduck released at the STAND pose; the 14 XL330 servos hold the HOME goals (no policy).

annotations.text: **microduck holding HOME.** Released 0.1 mm above the floor at the STAND pose, the 14 servos hold the HOME goals at kp 200 with no policy. HOME is balanced only by a policy that keeps balancing it: the robot sags into its backlash and its P gains and tips forward, past 40 deg after about 1.1 s (the microduck design notes report the same in their simulation). Only the soles touch the ground, so the run ends before the head would.

parameters.name: kp_fw
parameters.description: XL330 Position P Gain register (robotd gain 200; standing 0.8x, limp 50)

parameters.name: i_limit
parameters.description: Firmware current limit (BAM/training 1.75 A; impact-guard firmware on the robot 1.0 A)

parameters.name: t_latency
parameters.description: Command latency, goal written to goal applied (a multiple of 5 ms)

parameters.name: v_bat
parameters.description: Supply voltage (2S Li-ion: 8.2 V full, 7.4 V nominal, 6.6 V empty under load)

parameters.name: k_motor
parameters.description: Torque constant at the horn, also the back-EMF constant (BAM XL330 M6 fit)

parameters.name: r_motor
parameters.description: Winding plus driver resistance (BAM XL330 M6 fit)

parameters.name: armature
parameters.description: Rotor and gears reflected to the horn (BAM XL330 M6 fit); the rotor inertia of XL330 is armature/288.4^2, the joint of XL330Rigid carries it as Ja

parameters.name: r_bat
parameters.description: Battery + wiring resistance (assumed; training randomises the sag 0..0.2 V per N m)

options.text: No policy: the 14 servos hold the HOME pose and the robot tips forward within about a second, as the microduck notes say it does in their simulation. Raise the P gain and see how long it stays up. A run takes a few minutes.
